newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INL shares jump at open after W&H news.
newsitem.headline: INL shares jump at open after W&H news.

text.p: Shares in New Zealand publisher Independent Newspapers Ltd opened 25 cents higher at NZ$5.80 on Tuesday after Ireland's Independent Newspapers Plc launched a full takeover bid at $10.50/share for INL's rival Wilson and Horton Ltd.

Wilson and Horton gained $1.00 to $10.70 at the opening but on volume of just 250 shares. The company has advised shareholders not to sell pending further notice, and analysts said they expected an independent appraisal report to put a higher value on the shares.
"I think you'd be foolish to do anything with your stock prior to that independent report being available," said John Cairns, head of research at Cavill White Securities.
"Certainly it would be our thinking that the report would view this bid as being a bit on the light side, really."
Cairns said this was because the full benefits of some $120 million of investment in W&H's flagship newspaper "The New Zealand Herald" over the last 18 months had yet to kick in.
The group's newspaper operations were very strong and he expected the earnings potential to really start to show through over the next few halves.
Brokers said a successful takeover of W&H by Independent would leave INL as the main media play on the New Zealand stockmarket.

"The whole valuation attaching to the sector has been increased, so there'll be heightened interest there," said Cairns. After 15 minutes' trade, INL was up 30 cents to $5.85, but on volume of just 9,350 shares.
